conviction_note: Nothing company-level the wire does not already carry turned up: Q4 is fenced by the company's own $322-327M guide, which it has beaten in each of the last four quarters (known, and in the previews). The stock trades on active clients and the first FY27 guide, and last year that exact setup fell -16.5% on a revenue beat. What is left is a modest squeeze asymmetry: 11.9% of float short at 9.4 days to cover, still rising, a 52-week low, -14.6% over 20 days and -6% on print day, with call-heavy open interest. I size that below the finding (+0.8 finding, +0.5 emitted) because the line that sank last year's Q4 print, negative year-on-year client growth, is guided to still be negative this quarter.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue: company guide $322-327M (midpoint $324.5M), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1576942/000162828026042186/exhibit991-q326.htm (2026-06-10). Consensus $324.65M (Benzinga preview, https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/price-target/26/09/61835440/top-wall-street-forecasters-revamp-stitch-fix-expectations-ahead-of-q4-earnings) agrees with StockStory's +4.3% YoY on $311.2M = $324.6M (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/earnings-watch-stitch-fix-sfix-030900616.html). EPS consensus -$0.06. MarketBeat's $332M is an outlier and I disregard it. Q4 active clients guided -0.5% to -1% sequentially from 2.309M. FY27 has no guide and no reliable consensus I could source. The real bar is the FY27 guide, and UBS (2026-09-02) expects consensus near the top of whatever range is issued.
positioning_check: Short interest 13.36M shares, 11.9% of float, 9.38 days to cover, up 8.2% at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/sfix/short-interest via sweep, confirmed by MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/stitch-fix-nasdaqsfix-stock-price-down-49-heres-why-2026-08-11/, which shows 11.94% and the stock at $2.80, -6.19% on 2026-09-23). skew_25d is null in the baseline. Put/call OI ratio is 0.2 on 1,939 contracts (call-heavy). The event-implied move is 21.62% against a 10.54% median historical reaction. At 52-week low, -50% from the high, -14.6% over 20 days.

findings.finding: The short base is moderately crowded (11.9% of float, 9.4 days to cover) and grew 8.2% into the 2026-08-31 settlement. The stock went into the print at a fresh 52-week low ($2.80, -6.2% on the day, -13% over the month against -9% for the apparel group), and option open interest is 5:1 calls. So a clean beat-and-guide has squeeze fuel that a miss does not have in reverse.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's last seven reactions are +16.67, -2.37, +9.17, -16.49, -10.54, -5.44 and +44.35. The large up-moves (+44% Dec-2024, +16.7% Jun-2026) came when clients or guidance surprised from a depressed tape. The -16.49% on the 2025-09-24 Q4 print came despite a revenue beat ($311M vs $305M), because active clients fell ~8% YoY (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/09/25/why-stitch-fix-stock-was-plummeting-this-week/).
findings.source_date: 2026-09-23 (page shows the 2026-09-23 quote of $2.80, -6.19%, and short interest of 11.94% of float)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. A 21.6% implied move against a 10.5% median says the options market expects a large move but gives no direction, since skew is null. If shorts had already covered, short interest would have fallen into the print rather than risen 8.2%, and the stock would not be making lows on print day. What is not in the price is only the asymmetry, not a fact about the quarter.
findings.independence: The rising short interest has a second source in Equibles/Nasdaq at the 2026-08-31 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/sfix/short-interest). The call-heavy OI comes from the sealed baseline, not from a second document. Nothing company-level points the same way.

searched_and_found_nothing: Tariff and IEEPA refund angle. EDGAR full-text search for 'IEEPA' under CIK 1576942 returned 0 hits (2025-06 to 2026-09). The Q3 10-Q says 'tariffs have not materially impacted our cost of goods sold' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1576942/000162828026042504/sfix-20260502.htm). No refund line.

EDGAR since the Q3 print (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001576942.json). The only 8-K is a 2026-07-28 bylaw 5.03 aligning advance-notice provisions with Delaware case law. The 13Gs are passive: Renaissance 5.08% and Disciplined Growth Investors 16.0%. The Form 144 run is Anthony Bacos, a retiring CPTO whose retirement was announced 2026-03-12. CEO Baer's 2026-09-18 Form 4 is PSU tax withholding (code F), not a sale.

The Q3 10-Q shows a $32.0M securities class action settlement already accrued, $104.9M of buyback authorization remaining, $229.4M of cash with no debt, and the revolver extended to 2028. All of it is already disclosed. The buyback capacity is large against a ~$375M market cap, but nothing dates a new authorization inside the window.

Web traffic proxy: Similarweb (https://www.similarweb.com/website/stitchfix.com/) shows August traffic +6.84% MoM and global rank improving from #7,544 to #6,002 over three months, but paid search rose to 20.7% of desktop visits. I dropped it: it is a narrow proxy for clients the company has already guided, and the paid-search mix is consistent with UBS's 'higher promotional activity' risk, so its own evidence cuts both ways.
App, Reddit, Trustpilot, job postings (76 open roles, nothing structural) and the promo pages (the standard waived styling fee plus $20 off the first Fix): nothing new or unusual.

Peers in the preview (Movado, PVH) and the sell side (UBS cut its target to $4 on 2026-09-02, citing negative client growth and promotions; Telsey Hold $5 on 09-16; Northland Buy $5 on 09-18) are all in the wire.
baseline_tension: The one finding agrees with the run-up (a contrarian long into a drawdown), so it is close to the free control rather than beyond it. Against it sits the fact that the line this stock trades on, YoY active clients, is guided to be negative again, exactly as it was on last year's -16.5% Q4. So the emitted number sits below the finding and near zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (narrow proxy) and lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): dropped the Similarweb traffic finding (+0.8). It is a third-party proxy for clients the company already guided, and its own paid-search detail argued against it.

Lessons 1 and 6 (reaction function veto; a finding inside the guided range is expected): cut the positioning finding from +1.5 to +0.8. The Q4 revenue beat is inside a pattern the company has shown four quarters running, and this name sold a revenue beat by -16.5% last Q4 on the client line, which is guided negative again. print_vs_bar stays +1.5 while expected_move falls from +1.5 to +0.5.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the drawdown is partly explained (apparel group -9% over the month, the UBS risks), so no 'overreaction' finding was filed. Positioning is kept only as the information set that lesson names.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more) did not apply: I found no confirmed unpriced company-level number to size.
